4. API/interface changes to document
- No runtime API/interface changes; docs alignment only.
- README updates should explicitly document:
  - `workflow-log-analysis.yml` manual trigger + `codex_mode=true` path vs non-codex batch path
  - `comprehensive-test-and-release.yml` phase behavior
  - callback behavior when orchestrator project status is `complete` vs `failed`/`validation-failed`
  - timestamp-file fallback behavior (`since` when valid timestamp exists, else `lookback_days`)

5. Risks and edge cases to capture in docs
- Callback is poller-driven, not a separate phase job in `comprehensive-test-and-release.yml`.
- Callback dispatch only when status is `complete`; failure statuses send abort notification and do not dispatch release workflow.
- Callback can still be marked handled even on dispatch failure (prevents infinite redispatch loop); document as operational behavior.
- Invalid/missing `analysis/last_collection_timestamp.txt` falls back to `lookback_days`.
- Keep edits append-only around anchors; avoid reordering env-var bullets/table rows to prevent merge conflicts.

6. Testing/verification considerations
- Diff guard: only `README.md` and `agents.md` changed; no unrelated churn.
- Consistency checks after edit:
  - README workflow-log-analysis section matches current inputs (`since`, `lookback_days`, `codex_mode`, `batch_api_disabled`, `repos_override`)
  - README documents `analysis/last_collection_timestamp.txt` purpose
  - README and agents mention callback statuses and pending-label flow consistently
  - Env-var descriptions remain aligned; if unchanged behavior, no env-var table edits
- Final manual review: anchor-preserving edits and no renumbering/reflow outside touched doc blocks.

Conflicts detected between request wording and codebase
- “Callback behavior” is implemented in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`, not as a standalone callback phase/job in `.github/workflows/comprehensive-test-and-release.yml` (which currently has phases 1–3 only). Documentation should describe this explicitly to avoid implying nonexistent phase jobs.
